correctness.rationale: Dual to the equilateral free space is the oscillation norm N(f)=max_i f_i-min_i f_i on centered real m-vectors. Averaging any Hilbert comparison quadratic form over the coordinate-permutation group preserves distortion inequalities and makes Q(f)=c sum f_i^2 on the centered hyperplane globally optimal. On N(f)=1, min sum f_i^2=1/2 (two opposite half entries, remaining zero), while the maximum of centered sum squares is floor(m^2/4)/m by convexity of the centered quadratic on [0,1]^m and balancing binary vertices. Hence d_BM^2=max/min=2 floor(m^2/4)/m, and finite-dimensional duality transfers it back. m=2 yields 1; exact rational finite checks m=2..16 only corroborate the all-m proof.
residual_risks: Reproducible finite checks and existing verification logs never prove unbounded theorems; the above analytic argument supplies the proof.
